entry.title: Observed-analogue stress scenarios on scigrid-de (2015–2017 German stress days)
entry.summary: Three StormSpec scenarios replaying observed German stress days on the scigrid-de network, with precomputed PyPSA results.
entry.data_nature: StormSpec scenario inputs constructed by GridStorm from observed stress days (analogue mapping, not a real system state)

source.name: GridStorm observed-analogue scenarios (data/scenarios/observed/*.yaml)

license.name: Mixed: CC BY 4.0 demand multipliers (ENTSO-E load forecast); daily renewable multipliers derived from non-open ENTSO-E actual generation (derived-only)

source.attribution: Open Power System Data. 2020. Data Package Time series. Version 2020-10-06. https://doi.org/10.25832/time_series/2020-10-06. (Primary data from various sources, for a complete list see URL). German load forecast and load/generation: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform; German capacities: OPSD calculations based on BNetzA and netztransparenz.de. Day-ahead forecast of the total load per market time unit, Germany (Reg. (EU) 543/2013 Art. 6.1.b), ENTSO-E Transparency Platform (https://transparency.entsoe.eu/), obtained via Open Power System Data, Time series 2020-10-06 (https://doi.org/10.25832/time_series/2020-10-06), column DE_load_forecast_entsoe_transparency. Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) per the ENTSO-E list of data available for free re-use (2023-10-18), item #1. Changes made by GridStorm: the stress day's 24 hourly values are divided by the mean of the nearest 1 January (UTC), then by the scigrid-de network's normalized hourly load, and rounded to 4 decimals; only these ratios are published.

warnings: Metadata-only entry: the scenario files and results are linked, not re-published as series.
Renewable shortfall is one daily multiplier per carrier on the network's own 2011-01-01 profile; observed hourly renewable timing is not represented.

use_in_scenario.rationale: The three StormSpec analogue scenarios are published as PRECOMPUTED Studio presets on SciGRID-DE (too large for live runs on the free API); the presets are byte-identical copies of data/scenarios/observed/*.yaml. The other two are observed-high-load-low-res-2017-01-24 and observed-peak-load-2017-12-13.

entry.description:
Historical-analogue scenarios: the German highest-load day, the winter Dunkelflaute day and the combined high-load / low-renewable day (detected in OPSD 2015–2020) mapped onto the 24 snapshots of scigrid-de: hourly demand from the CC BY 4.0 load forecast, one MODELED daily availability multiplier per renewable carrier. The mapping and every result are **modeled** (DC LOPF, 2011 topology), not a reconstruction of the day.

Precomputed results (`data/observed/analogue-results.json`):

| Scenario | Day (UTC) | Unserved energy (MWh) | Peak shed (MW) | Shed hours |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline (network day, no events) | 2011-01-01 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `observed-dunkelflaute-2015-01-20` | 2015-01-20 | 2,721 | 230 | 17 |
| `observed-high-load-low-res-2017-01-24` | 2017-01-24 | 4,731 | 346 | 20 |
| `observed-peak-load-2017-12-13` | 2017-12-13 | 4,429 | 335 | 19 |

transformations.description: stress days from OPSD actual load / generation / capacity (dates only are committed)
hourly demand multipliers from the load forecast; one daily renewable multiplier per carrier, rounded to 0.05

spec.name: SciGRID Germany — baseline day
spec.description: Reference dispatch of the PyPSA SciGRID-DE example (585 buses, 852 lines, 96 transformers, 38 pumped-hydro storage units) for 2011-01-01, 24 hourly snapshots, no crisis events.

spec.name: Observed analogue: combined high-load / low-renewable day 2017-01-24 (Germany, OPSD/ENTSO-E)
spec.description: Historical-analogue scenario. The German combined high-load / low-renewable day 2017-01-24 (UTC), detected objectively in Open Power System Data time series 2020-10-06 (lowest daily-mean wind+solar CF among complete UTC days whose daily-mean load >= the 0.90 quantile of daily-mean load), is mapped onto the 24 snapshots of scigrid-de (2011-01-01 00:00-23:00 UTC): hour by hour, the ENTSO-E day-ahead load forecast's shape and level relative to the reference day 2017-01-01 (CC BY 4.0); for wind onshore / wind offshore / solar, one MODELED daily availability multiplier per carrier (the day's renewable shortfall, rounded to 0.05) on the network's own hourly profiles. The mapping and every result are MODELED. Generated by pipelines/observed (gridstorm_observed.build) - do not edit.
assumptions: Demand input (CC BY 4.0): Day-ahead forecast of the total load per market time unit, Germany (Reg. (EU) 543/2013 Art. 6.1.b), ENTSO-E Transparency Platform (https://transparency.entsoe.eu/), obtained via Open Power System Data, Time series 2020-10-06 (https://doi.org/10.25832/time_series/2020-10-06), column DE_load_forecast_entsoe_transparency. Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) per the ENTSO-E list of data available for free re-use (2023-10-18), item #1. Changes made by GridStorm: the stress day's 24 hourly values are divided by the mean of the nearest 1 January (UTC), then by the scigrid-de network's normalized hourly load, and rounded to 4 decimals; only these ratios are published.

Stress-day selection: the date was chosen in OPSD actual load and wind/solar generation and capacity (ENTSO-E Reg. 543/2013 Art. 6.1.a and 16.1; OPSD calculations based on BNetzA and netztransparenz.de). Those series are not openly licensed; GridStorm stores no value or statistic derived from them except the date and the coarse daily renewable multipliers below (data/observed/opsd-de/manifest.json, source.column_reuse).

Time alignment: network snapshot h = UTC hour h of the stress day. Evidence (data/observed/opsd-de/derived-multipliers.json, alignment_evidence): the network's solar availability matches observed 1 January solar CF far better in UTC than shifted to local time; for load the evidence is weaker.

MODELED demand mapping, applied uniformly to every load: m_h = [F(d,h) / mean_h F(ref,h)] / [L_net(h) / mean_h L_net(h)], F = day-ahead load forecast, reference day ref = 2017-01-01 (the 1 January nearest to d, i.e. the analogue of the network's own 1 January profile). The scaled network load follows the forecast stress-day shape and its level relative to a 1 January; the actual load differs from the forecast by the forecast error. Multipliers rounded to 4 decimals; clipped to (0, 5] at hours [none].

MODELED renewable shortfall per carrier c (Wind Onshore, Wind Offshore, Solar), applied to every generator of c for the whole day: w_c = min(round(mean_h CF_obs,c / mean_h CF_net,c / 0.05) * 0.05, 1), CF_obs = national generation / national capacity, CF_net = capacity-weighted p_max_pu of the network's generators of c. The hourly shape stays the network's own 2011-01-01 shape; the observed hourly profile is deliberately not reproduced (not openly licensed). No event when w = 1. Wind Onshore w = 0.05; Wind Offshore w = 0.15; Solar w = 0.20.
Aggregate national profiles are applied uniformly to every bus/generator: the spatial pattern of load and of wind/solar availability remains the network's 2011-01-01 pattern; only levels change.

The network (2011 grid topology, 2014 renewable capacities, 2011 demand profile) differs from the observed year's system; installed capacities are NOT rescaled. This is an analogue stress test, not a reconstruction of the observed day.

items.name: SciGRID Germany (PyPSA example)
items.description: German 220/380 kV transmission grid from SciGRID v0.2 (derived from OpenStreetMap), with power plants, load and renewable availability for 24 hourly snapshots of 2011-01-01, as packaged by the PyPSA project (pypsa.examples.scigrid_de).

cost_basis.provenance: PyPSA v1.4.0 scigrid-de example uses illustrative per-carrier marginal costs; the upstream scigrid-lopf-then-pf notebook says these are not accurate.
assumptions: Example costs are placeholders, not market prices or a verified currency basis.
Only runs on this same example cost basis are monetarily comparable.
VOLL is a scenario penalty in illustrative cost units/MWh, not an economic outage-damage estimate.
